identificationCriteria.rendered:
## Evidence significance

A useful evidence entity is a diagram-relevant concept grounded in the supplied
documents. It helps explain the requested chronology, argument, relationship,
event, decision, or recurring theme.

An evidence entity may cover multiple related passages when they collectively
support one concept. Give each entity a concise label and summary and exact
corpus-relative document ranges. Descriptions must stay within what those
passages support.

Strong candidates include claims, decisions, events, actors, definitions,
contrasts, causal links, and transitions that connect the requested diagram
concepts.

compactionCriteria.rendered:
## Evidence presentation

Preserve the meaningful statements, surrounding context, chronology, and
relationships in each cited passage while omitting unrelated detail.

For every evidence range, provide a continuous compactedSource presentation.
Retained sections quote the relevant document lines. Collapsed-comment sections
summarize only material supported by their exact span using concise 7-bit ASCII.
Map each semantic summary node to the exact lines that support it. Blank and
connector-only lines have no mapping.

The server snapshots the original document lines after validating every
submitted coordinate.

contextPrompt.rendered:
Collect evidence entities for "MARKDOWN Plan Implementation Call Graph".

Request:
Read MARKDOWN.md and collect source-backed evidence for one implementation call graph of the Compositional Domain Architecture Plan. Trace dependency and execution order from characterization through per-DiagramSet DomainProfile composition, corpus and evidence facades, recipe and surface registries, generic highlights, the representation graph, stable element indexes, scoped agent progress, compatibility adapters, migrations, acceptance gates, and final cleanup. Capture branch points and the contracts passed between phases; map every graph node to exact MARKDOWN.md line ranges. Favor implementation/control dependencies over restating every interface field.

## Identify Evidence

Inspect the documents and identify concepts that satisfy these criteria:

## Evidence significance

A useful evidence entity is a diagram-relevant concept grounded in the supplied
documents. It helps explain the requested chronology, argument, relationship,
event, decision, or recurring theme.

An evidence entity may cover multiple related passages when they collectively
support one concept. Give each entity a concise label and summary and exact
corpus-relative document ranges. Descriptions must stay within what those
passages support.

Strong candidates include claims, decisions, events, actors, definitions,
contrasts, causal links, and transitions that connect the requested diagram
concepts.

For each match, return its classification, concise label and summary, optional
document symbol or timestamp, and exact corpus-relative evidence ranges.

## Present Evidence

Create a compactedSource evidence presentation for every identified document
range, following these criteria:

## Evidence presentation

Preserve the meaningful statements, surrounding context, chronology, and
relationships in each cited passage while omitting unrelated detail.

For every evidence range, provide a continuous compactedSource presentation.
Retained sections quote the relevant document lines. Collapsed-comment sections
summarize only material supported by their exact span using concise 7-bit ASCII.
Map each semantic summary node to the exact lines that support it. Blank and
connector-only lines have no mapping.

The server snapshots the original document lines after validating every
submitted coordinate.

Return retained passage sections, collapsed-comment sections, and exact
evidence-node mappings.

## Submission

Submit all identified evidence entities together.

Finish by calling submit_code_entities. If the submission is rejected, correct the reported issues and call it again.
